name: Document page
markup: No html in this file. Each variant below carries the path to its own markup at r/document-page/<variant>.html — fetch the one you need.
description: The record as a sheet of paper: a purchase order, a GST tax invoice, a delivery challan, a goods receipt note. Laid out on A4, printed from the browser, and built so that what comes out of the printer is the same document that was on screen.
when_to_use: A record that leaves the building — the purchase order a vendor is sent, the tax invoice an auditor will ask for later, the delivery challan that travels with the lorry, the goods receipt note the store files. The screen where that record is worked on is record-page: the header, the status, the tabs, the timeline and the buttons that change it. This is the artefact record-page produces, and the two are not one screen in two modes — record-page is arranged for the buyer amending the order, and this is arranged for a transporter at a gate, a vendor's accounts clerk and an assessing officer three years later, none of whom has a toolbar, a hover or a second click. Reach for card when the thing is a panel grouping one region of a screen; a card is furniture and this is the whole page. Reach for table when rows are read, sorted and paged on screen — a printed line table has different rules, it may not restack into cards, it repeats its own header across sheets and its totals may not be orphaned, and those rules live here rather than in table. The test is where the pixels end up: if the answer is a printer, a courier or a PDF attached to an email, it is this.
rules: It renders inside app-shell like every other signed-in page, and the shell is chrome. Everything that is not the sheet — the toolbar, the copy selector, the back link — carries print:hidden, and what is left on the paper is the document. app-shell's own rail and topbar do not carry print:hidden today, so a document printed from inside the shell as it stands comes out with the navigation down the left of it. That is a gap in app-shell and closing it is a decision for a person, not something this entry patches from the outside.

Backgrounds do not print. Chrome, Firefox and Edge drop every background fill unless somebody ticks Background graphics in the print dialog, and nobody ticks it. So nothing on the sheet may carry meaning in a fill: structure is borders and rules, the recessed table header keeps bg-zinc-50 for the screen but earns its shape from a border-y that survives without it, and the status dot — a 6px background circle — is not drawn on a document at all. A document says Approved in a word. This is the one screen in the system where the locked status pill is the wrong component.

A watermark is the same defect twice over. DRAFT set diagonally in pale grey is a background effect in a colour chosen to be faint, so it prints as nothing on a laser and as a smear on an inkjet, and the sheet that comes out looks exactly like the real one. The draft variant states it in a ruled band of type above the letterhead, where it cannot be dropped and cannot be missed.

Rules that have to survive paper stop at border-zinc-300. The Divider token, border-zinc-100, is a 4% grey and is simply not there on a printed sheet; border-zinc-200 is marginal and is used only for the row rules inside a line table, where the rows are close enough together that the eye supplies the rest. Hierarchy comes from weight — border-b-2 under the letterhead, border-t-2 over the totals — and not from a darker colour, because the system has no ink-weight border token. That is a real gap and this entry left it open rather than inventing one.

Physical size is @page, and @page is not a utility. A4 is 210 by 297mm: the sheet is max-w-[210mm] with min-h-[297mm] so the screen preview is the shape of the paper, and print:min-h-0 because the printable area is 297mm less the page margin — a 297mm minimum on paper pushes a blank second sheet out of every one-page document. The margin itself, @page { size: A4; margin: 14mm 12mm }, cannot be written as a Tailwind class and belongs once in the project stylesheet. The preview variant carries the rule to copy.

Do not trust a breakpoint to mean paper. A4 portrait is 794 CSS px at 96dpi, so md: applies while printing and lg: does not — but the Scale field in the print dialog changes the layout width, and at 50% the same sheet lays out at about 1588px with every lg: rule switched on. Where the printed shape has to differ from the screen, write print: and let it win. A table that only becomes a table at md is a stack of cards on somebody's paper.

The line table is the one region here allowed to scroll sideways at 390px, inside its own overflow-x-auto box, and it is cancelled again with md:overflow-visible print:overflow-visible. Both halves matter. A preview that restacks the lines into cards is a preview of something that will never come out of the printer, which is the whole reason the exception is taken. And an element with overflow other than visible is monolithic in paged media, so a line table left inside a live scroller is clipped at the first page break instead of splitting across sheets. The same trap makes overflow-hidden rounded-xl — the card idiom every other panel in this system uses — wrong on a document. The exception used to cost an affordance — at 390px the line table simply looked cut off at the right edge. The framework has an answer for that now and this entry takes it: the scroller carries relative, tabindex='0', role='region' and a name, so it is reachable and announced, and a line under it says it scrolls. relative is not cosmetic there: an sr-only span inside a scroller with no positioned ancestor resolves against the document and widens the page, which is a 390px overflow with no visible cause.

A table splits across sheets by itself and repeats its <thead> while it does, because display: table-header-group is the browser's own default for a real <thead>. It stops the moment the table is wrapped in a flex or grid container, a transform, or a scroller. break-inside-avoid goes on every <tr>: a row split across the fold is not a shorter row, it is two rows carrying half a figure each.

Nothing that adds up may be orphaned. break-inside-avoid on the tax summary, on the amount in words, on each signature block and on the foot. A totals block that lands on a sheet of its own with no lines above it is a defect the reader cannot detect, because it reads as a total of what is on that sheet.

Page numbers and carried-forward subtotals are the view's job, not the browser's. counter(page) inside an @page margin box is not implemented in Chrome, and no CSS anywhere can sum the lines that fell on the sheet before. So a document that needs "Page 2 of 3" and a brought-forward figure is paginated on the server into one <section> per sheet, each ending in break-after-page — that is multi-page. Where neither is needed, do not paginate: let the table flow and repeat its own header, which is purchase-order.

Nothing inside the sheet is sticky. position: sticky is meaningless on paper and actively wrong on the way there — a sticky header prints on the first sheet and leaves a gap on the rest. The toolbar above the sheet is sticky, and it is print:hidden.

Corners are square. rounded-xl is the panel affordance of a screen; a printed form is ruled boxes, and one rounded box among them reads as a screenshot pasted into a document. The sheet keeps rounded-xl on screen, because there it is the edge of the paper, and drops it with print:rounded-none.

Secondary text on the sheet stops at zinc-600. zinc-500 and lighter are screen-chrome colours: at 11px through an office laser they read as grey mush. The one place zinc-500 is used here is a footer line nobody has to read.

Figures carry two decimal places and Indian grouping — ₹5,26,080.00. The registers drop the paise because in a column of forty they are noise; on a tax document they are the amount, and dropping them makes the sheet disagree with the ledger by up to fifty paise a line. Every figure keeps tabular-nums, and an identifier — GSTIN, HSN, e-way bill, PO number — is never truncated, because a shortened identifier is a different identifier and somebody will read it into a phone.

The values are the server's. Nothing on the sheet is computed in the browser, which is the line between this and form-page: a rail that recomputes is helping somebody fill a form, and a document that recomputes is a second implementation of the tax engine whose output the vendor and the assessing officer read. The only Alpine on these variants is in the chrome — which copies to print, and the button that calls print().

anatomy.description: The zinc-100 page the sheet sits on, so the preview reads as paper on a desk. print:bg-white print:p-0 — on paper there is no desk, and a ground that survives printing is a full-bleed grey rectangle nobody asked for.

One A4 page: max-w-[210mm], min-h-[297mm] on screen, print:min-h-0 print:rounded-none print:border-0 print:p-0. The border and the rounded corner are the edge of the paper drawn for the screen; on paper the edge is the paper.
Who is issuing the document — name, address, GSTIN, CIN, telephone — under a border-b-2. The mark beside it is a bordered square, not a filled one, because a filled square prints as white.
The document type as the h1, the number under it, the date and the revision. Top right, because that is where every clerk who handles the sheet looks first.
Two square bordered boxes side by side: who it is addressed to and where the goods go. Each carries the GSTIN and the state code, because the state codes are what decide the tax split.
A <dl> of the four or five terms that qualify the whole document — required by, payment terms, freight, buyer reference. One bordered band, two columns on a phone and four from sm.

A real <table> inside overflow-x-auto md:overflow-visible print:overflow-visible. <thead> repeats across sheets by itself; every <tr> takes break-inside-avoid; the foot totals the column it sits under and leaves a mixed-unit quantity column as an em dash.
The legally controlling figure, spelled out, in a bordered box with break-inside-avoid. It is text in the reading order, never decoration and never aria-hidden.

The build-up from taxable value to the round-off and the total, as its own small table beside the words. break-inside-avoid: a tax block split across sheets is a tax block that has to be added up twice.

Original for Recipient, Duplicate for Transporter, Triplicate for Supplier — a word in a bordered box at the head of the sheet. Text, because a tint would print as nothing and all three copies would then be identical.
Two, at the foot, each break-inside-avoid: who prepared it and who signs for the company. The rule to sign over is a border-t, never a run of underscores, which is read out as punctuation.
The computer-generated note and "Page 1 of 1". The date and URL a browser prints down the margin come from the print dialog, not from here, and nothing in the page can remove them.
The screen chrome above the sheet: back, Print, Download PDF, which copies. print:hidden, and it is the only part of the page carrying state.

behaviour: Nothing on the sheet moves. It has no disclosure, no sort, no hover state and no tooltip, because every one of those is a promise that the paper cannot keep. Everything that moves is in the toolbar above it.

Print calls window.print() on the page that is already on screen. It does not open a second window and it does not re-render the document into a hidden frame — the sheet the user checked is the sheet that has to go to the printer, and a second render is a second chance for the two to disagree.

Download PDF is a server route that returns a file, not window.print() renamed. The browser's Save as PDF and a server-rendered PDF are different documents with different fonts and different page breaks, and a vendor who receives one and an auditor who receives the other will find the difference.

The copy selector adds hidden to a copy rather than filtering it out of the record. Unticking Triplicate takes it off the paper and off the screen at once, so the count in the toolbar and the sheets below it cannot disagree.
Each copy and each sheet ends in break-after-page except the last one, which ends in nothing. break-after-page on the final section prints a blank sheet at the end of every job.

At 390px the toolbar wraps to two rows, the sheet fills the width, and the line table scrolls sideways inside its own box. Everything below the table — the amount in words, the tax summary, the terms, the signatures — is full width and reachable without scrolling, because those are the parts somebody checks on a phone.

A document produced from a record that is not approved prints as a draft: the band at the head, no signature block, and the number shown as not yet allotted. It is a state the record can be in, not a preview mode the user chooses.

The browser's own page header and footer — the URL, the date, the page numbers down the margin — are switched off in the print dialog and nowhere else. No CSS in this page can remove them, so the sheet carries its own page numbering rather than relying on the browser's.
accessibility: One <main>, one <h1> naming the document and its number, and an h2 on every region — Vendor, Deliver to, Order lines, Tax summary, Terms. Several of those h2s render at 11px uppercase; heading level is what a screen reader plans the document with and has nothing to do with size.

Where one page carries three copies, the h1 belongs to the page and each copy is a <section> with an accessible name whose own headings start at h2. Three h1s on one page is three documents and the outline says nothing about which is which.

On a paginated document the h1 is on the first sheet only. Continuation sheets carry a compact head at h2 naming the document and the sheet number, which is how a paper continuation sheet has always been headed.

The line table has an sr-only <caption> saying what it lists and against what, <th scope="col"> on every heading, and <th scope="row"> on the foot total. A bare figure at the bottom of a table is announced as a number with no word attached to it.

The copy marking is text. It is the only thing separating three otherwise identical sheets, so it cannot live in a fill or a border colour — neither of which is available to a screen reader or to a laser printer.

The amount in words stays in the reading order at full contrast. It is the figure that controls if the digits and the words disagree, and it is the line a reader who cannot scan a column of numerals uses.
The rule above a signature caption is a border, never a run of underscores. A row of underscores is announced as punctuation, one character at a time.
The letterhead mark is aria-hidden. The company name is beside it in text, and a bordered letter K adds nothing to what is already said.

Toolbar controls are real buttons with names that say what they do — Print this order, Download as PDF — and they wear focus-visible:outline-3 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-zinc-700/15 like everything else. Print is a button, not a link: it changes nothing and goes nowhere.
Nothing on the page is autofocused. The document is there to be read from the top, and an autofocused Print button turns a stray Enter left over from the previous screen into a print job.
